content.text:
Your second idea is the right one, and it's stronger than you framed it. Today's flow throws away information and then tries to recover it:

```
engine → terminal writer → ANSI string → image.go re-parses ANSI → pixels
```

`image.go` re-derives what the writer already computed. [image.go:498](src/cli/image/image.go:498) — *"Add additional width for Nerd Font glyphs"* — is a symptom: [terminal/writer.go:894](src/terminal/writer.go:894) already ran `countVisibleCells` through `go-runewidth`, and the imager redoes it worse. Every fidelity bug in the imager lives in that round-trip.

## But it isn't "add a writer" — there's no writer abstraction to add to

`terminal` is a 1243-line package with **global mutable state**: `builder`, `length`, `cellIndex`, `foregroundColor`, `currentColor`, `bgGradientCells`. `Write(bg, fg, txt)` appends into a package-level `strings.Builder`. Escape emission is interleaved with the logic that decides what to draw — `writeColorise`, `writeTransparentStart`, `writeEscapedAnsiParts` all bake `\x1b[` into the same pass as anchor scanning and gradient stamping.

So the actual move is one step earlier: **separate what to draw from how to encode it.**

```
engine
  → resolver   anchors, gradients, transparency, hyperlinks, cell widths
  → Run stream []Run{Text, FG, BG, Style, Link}
  → encoder    ansi | svg | json | plain
```

The resolver already exists inside the writer — `activeBackground()`, `activeForeground()`, `gradientCell()`, `countVisibleCells()`, `writeAnchorOverride()`. It just never surfaces its answers.

Extract the run stream and you get four encoders for the price of one:

- **ansi** — current behavior, must stay byte-identical
- **svg** — replaces all 920 lines of `image.go`, drops `gg`, `stackblur`, `opentype`, `freetype`, and the runtime Hack.zip download
- **json** — free, and it's exactly what the studio and any render endpoint want
- **plain** — currently a `Plain bool` threaded through the same pass; becomes an encoder

Window chrome isn't a reason to keep `image.go`: title bar, dots and author line are SVG decoration, and `stackblur` existed only for the drop shadow, which is `feDropShadow`.

## What stays worth having in the binary

One thing, and it's real: `config export image` **without** `--data` renders *your actual environment* — your repo, your cloud context, your paths. A generic web builder can only render a config someone hands it. That's the difference between "screenshot my prompt" and "preview this theme".

Everything else is a pure function of config, and pure functions of config belong on the web. So the split falls out naturally:

- **binary** — renders live state, offline, no deps (with the SVG encoder)
- **web** — renders shared configs, gallery, studio

Both run the same resolver. Neither needs a second implementation.

## Honest cost

**ANSI output is the product.** A byte-identical refactor of the hot path is the risk, not the SVG encoder. Before touching anything, build the net: render all 124 bundled themes with `--data segment_data.json`, snapshot the ANSI as golden files, diff on every commit. You have `writer_test.go`, `writer_gradient_test.go`, `writer_hyperlink_test.go` — good coverage of the mechanisms, but not of real-world combinations.

**Perf is the thing to watch, not correctness.** This is the prompt-render path and speed is your headline claim. Materializing `[]Run` per segment adds allocations. Two ways out: pool the slice, or have the encoder consume runs via callback so nothing is materialized. Gate the whole refactor on benchstat against the existing hot-path benchmarks — a regression here is worse than the current duplication.

**Global state is the tedious part.** Turning package globals into a struct is mechanical but touches every call site in `prompt/`. Bigger diff than the encoding work.

## Suggested staging

1. Golden-file harness over all bundled themes. Land it alone, no behavior change.
2. Extract the run stream behind the existing `terminal.Write` API; ANSI encoder consumes it. Prove byte-identical + no benchstat regression.
3. Add the SVG encoder. `config export image --format svg`.
4. Switch the gallery to SVG. 8MB of PNG → a few hundred KB.
5. Delete `image.go` and its four dependencies.
6. JSON encoder + `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` — that's the studio, and by then it's nearly free.

Steps 1–2 are the whole risk. 3 onward are additive.

But if we have an SVG renderer that is pretty fast and works with data only, which is a good idea, there's no reason to have any JSON output or have the web render anything differently. That can just live in the function, return the SVG immediately based on the config that was provided with a predefined set of data, and we're done.

Agreed. Drop the JSON encoder — it was solving a problem SVG doesn't have.

**SVG is already structured output.** Emit the grouping you'd have put in JSON:

```xml
<g data-block="0" data-segment="git" data-type="scm">
  <rect …/><text …>main ≡ +2</text>
</g>
```

Now the studio can hit-test a click to a segment, highlight on hover, and scroll the editor to the right node — straight from the DOM, no parallel format, no drift between "what was rendered" and "what was described". That was the only thing JSON bought.

And pinning the data file in the Function isn't just simplification — it's the SSRF guard falling out of the design for free. No live segment resolution possible, because there's no path to it.

## Three things still worth deciding

**1. Fonts, which have three different right answers.**

| Context | Strategy |
|---|---|
| Local `--format svg` | Reference `"Hack Nerd Font"` by family. User has it — that's why they run omp. Tiny file. |
| Site gallery / studio | Reference a site-hosted subset woff2. Crisp, one download, cached across 124 themes. |
| Shared output (README, blog, Discord) | Embed a subset as data URI, **or** rasterize. Otherwise a viewer without the font gets tofu. |

That third row is the one that bites. GitHub renders SVG in markdown but the reader's machine resolves the font — a powerline README on a stock laptop becomes boxes. Today's PNG is immune to that, which is a real thing people rely on.

**2. So keep exactly one raster path — in the Function.**

`resvg-wasm` or `sharp`, SVG→PNG, behind `?format=png`. Not in the binary. `oh-my-posh config export image --format png` becomes a POST, or you tell people to use the endpoint URL directly. Either way the four Go deps and the Hack.zip download still leave.

**3. Cache it.**

Config → SVG is a pure function. Key on `hash(config) + data version + renderer version`, immutable, long TTL. The gallery becomes 124 cache hits and the studio pays the round trip only on genuinely new configs.

## Where that leaves the plan

```
resolver (Go)  →  SVG encoder  →  ┬─ binary, local, live env
                                   ├─ Function, pinned data, config in / SVG out
                                   └─ Function + resvg → PNG when asked
```

WASM is still worth doing eventually, but it's now purely a latency optimization for the studio — same encoder, same output, no round trip. Not a different architecture, so it can wait until the studio proves it needs it.

Revised staging:

1. Golden-file harness over all 124 bundled themes.
2. Extract the run stream; ANSI encoder byte-identical, no benchstat regression.
3. SVG encoder with `data-*` annotations. `config export image --format svg`.
4. Function: config in, SVG out, pinned data, cached. Point the gallery at it.
5. Delete `image.go`, `gg`, `stackblur`, `opentype`, `freetype`, the font download.
6. `?format=png` via resvg for the README case.
7. WASM only if studio latency demands it.

Steps 1–2 remain the whole risk. Everything after is additive.

in that case, if we have this, I would only render or add that logic to the build we need for the website and the function, and never in the artifacts we use, unless the diff is really significant and we remove more lines than we add by changing the direction. It doesn't really matter, to be honest.

Your condition is already met. Measured:

**Removed**
| | lines |
|---|---|
| `cli/image/image.go` | 920 |
| `cli/image/fonts.go` | 95 |
| `cli/image/config.go` | 98 |
| tests (`image_test.go`, `config_test.go`) | 764 |
| **total** | **~1,877** |

Plus three direct dependencies used **nowhere else in the codebase** — `fogleman/gg`, `esimov/stackblur-go`, `golang.org/x/image` — and `golang/freetype` goes with them as indirect. Plus the runtime Hack.zip download from GitHub.

**Added**: an SVG encoder over the run stream. Grid geometry, one advance constant, rects + text, chrome wrapper, `feDropShadow`. ~300–400 lines, and you can keep `cli/image/config.go` as-is if you want the same `--settings` file format, which shrinks it further.

Net roughly **−1,500 lines, −3 deps, −1 network call**, and the shipped binary gets *smaller*. So don't build-tag it. Ship it everywhere.

The build-tag path would have cost you a doubled CI matrix, a second artifact to explain, and a stripped binary where `config export image` errors out — support burden for no gain when the alternative is a net deletion.

## The one genuine user-facing change

PNG output. Today `config export image` writes a PNG locally; after this it can't, because the rasterizer is what's being deleted. That's a behavior change people have in scripts and CI.

Cleanest handling:

```bash
oh-my-posh config export image --config x.omp.json              # writes .svg now
oh-my-posh config export image --config x.omp.json --format png # errors with a pointer
```

Give it a deprecation window: keep `--format png` working via the endpoint (opt-in, prints where the config is going), warn for a release or two, then drop the flag. Worth a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer when the default flips — it's user-facing output behavior, not an internal signature.

The README-tofu case from earlier is what `--format png` exists for, so it shouldn't vanish entirely — it just moves to the Function.

## Revised plan

1. Golden-file harness over all 124 bundled themes.
2. Extract the run stream. ANSI encoder byte-identical, benchstat clean.
3. SVG encoder with `data-*` annotations, in the normal build.
4. `--format svg` default; `--format png` warns and routes to the endpoint.
5. Delete `cli/image/`, drop the three deps and the font download.
6. Function: config in, SVG out, pinned data, cached. Gallery switches, 8MB of PNG goes away.
7. WASM only if studio latency demands it.

Still analysis only — nothing written. Want me to plan step 1 and 2 properly, or start with the Phase 0 website bug fixes from the artifact, which are independent of all this?

start with the phase 0 website fixes, build a good plan, review the plan with Fable, and do the execution with Sonnet 5 in parallel where you can. And for the website design, I actually prefer the visual appearance of direction A. It's a lot cleaner, together with the segment catalog and the studio direction of B.

1	# Phase 3 — Delegate
2	
3	Match the executor to the task, not the other way around. The point is cost and speed without
4	losing quality — the coordinator stays accountable for the result.
5	
6	## Executor matrix
7	
8	Tier definitions and per-vendor model examples: [model-tiers.md](model-tiers.md).
9	
10	| Task profile                                             | Executor                                                       |
11	| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
12	| Trivial: mechanical edit, config tweak, typo, doc update  | Do it directly, or batch on a trivial-tier model              |
13	| Standard, well-specified implementation                   | Coordinator itself, or a same-tier subagent for parallelism   |
14	| Hits an escalation trigger (see [escalate.md](escalate.md)) | Escalation-tier subagent, for that one specific question    |
15	
16	- The coordinator typically runs at implementer tier itself, so standard tasks are usually
17	  executed directly rather than delegated. Delegate anyway when there's real parallelism —
18	  independent tasks, each in its own worktree — or to shed trivial mechanical work onto a
19	  cheaper model.
20	- Escalation is never the default path for "ambiguous" or "architectural" — it fires only on the
21	  concrete triggers in [escalate.md](escalate.md), and only for the specific question, not the
22	  whole task.
23	
24	## What a delegation carries
25	
26	Hand the subagent its full pinned spec from Phase 2, plus:
27	
28	- The verification commands it must run and pass before reporting done.
29	- The instruction to report what it changed and what it verified — not just "done".
30	- The instruction to stop and report when it hits something the spec does not cover, instead of
31	  improvising scope.
32	
33	## What is never delegated downward
34	
35	Analysis, final verification, and delivery never go to an implementer — they stay with the
36	coordinator or go up to Escalation tier for a specific question:
37	
38	- Analysis and root-cause work (Phase 1).
39	- Final verification (Phase 5) — an implementer's green run is a claim, not a result.
40	- Commits, history rewrites, pushes, and user-facing reporting (Phase 6) — these stay with the
41	  coordinator regardless of tier; they're about accountability, not capability, so they never go
42	  to Escalation tier either.

---
name: website-redesign-direction
description: Chosen ohmyposh.dev redesign direction — Direction A visuals, faceted segment catalog, studio; SVG encoder replaces the PNG imager
metadata:
  type: project
---

On 2026-07-26 Jan picked the ohmyposh.dev redesign direction after a competitor sweep of
12 dev-tool sites: **Direction A's visual language** (light-first, calibrated blue
`#1f6fd0`, Docusaurus bones kept — "a lot cleaner"), combined with **Direction B's
faceted segment catalog** and **the studio direction**. Directions B (dark-first,
powerline-chevron geometry) and C (dark studio) were rejected as whole visual systems;
only their structural ideas carry over.

Companion architecture decision, same session: the theme/segment previews stop being
PNGs. `cli/image/image.go` (920 lines, plus `gg` / `stackblur` / `x/image` / `freetype`
and a runtime Hack.zip download) gets replaced by an **SVG encoder** sitting behind an
extracted run stream in the `terminal` package — sibling to the ANSI encoder, not a
consumer of its output. No JSON encoder: SVG carries `data-segment` / `data-block`
attributes, so it already is the structured format. Net ≈ −1,500 lines, so it ships in
the normal binary rather than behind a build tag.

Agreed staging: golden-file harness over all 124 bundled themes → extract run stream
(ANSI byte-identical, benchstat clean) → SVG encoder → Function renders config to SVG
with a pinned data file → delete `cli/image/` → `?format=png` via resvg for GitHub
READMEs → WASM only if studio latency demands it.

**Why:** the redesign and the renderer work are the same project — the gallery, the
segment catalog and the studio all consume one renderer, so the visual direction and the
encoder decision constrain each other.

**How to apply:** when website or imager work resumes, treat Direction A as settled and
do not re-pitch dark-first. Phase 0 (website bug fixes) is separate and was executed
first; see [[project-knowledge-skill]] for accumulated website gotchas.

Related: [[template-data-feature]] — `--data` replay is what makes the engine hermetic
enough to run in a Function or in WASM.

Drop `hero--primary`, drop the `#173448` background, drop the rules that force the hero title and subtitle white. The hero sits on the normal page background in both colour modes. 2. **`hero.png` stays.** It is a 1100x44 strip showing the **default** prompt — what you get from `oh-my-posh init` with no `--config`. It is not the `jandedobbeleer` theme. Do not replace it, do not hand-author a substitute, do not caption it as a named theme. Phase 2's SVG encoder replaces it. 3. **The install box is the hero's primary action**, built from `@theme/Tabs`, `@theme/TabItem` and `@theme/CodeBlock`. `CodeBlock` already ships a copy button and `Tabs` already persists the choice by `groupId`, so no custom JS and no new dependency. 4. **No version number in the button.** It would need a GitHub release lookup at build time. Not worth the moving part in this phase. 5. **The announcement bar is removed entirely** (Jan's call). Sponsorship moves to the footer, which gains a dedicated Sponsor group. 6. **Sponsor and Swag leave the navbar.** Primary nav becomes Docs, Segments, Themes, Blog. Both keep footer placement. 7. **The homepage's "180+" claim becomes 117**, matching the documented segment count already corrected in Phase 0. 8. **No new pages.** No `/community`, no segment catalog, no theme gallery. content.text:
All verified against build output. Cascade order confirmed correct: Infima's light default at byte 1849, ours at 14512, dark ramp at 53627.

One correction to Fable's reasoning worth noting: Infima *does* define `--ifm-button-background-color: transparent` for `.button--outline`, so the bare outline button's border was not actually collapsing. Adding `button--primary` is still the right call — it gives the button an accent border and correct hover in both modes — but the stated cause was wrong. The `color: #fff` diagnosis was correct: `.button--outline:not(.button--active):not(:hover){color:var(--ifm-font-color-base)}` is exactly what the Phase 0 override was defeating.

mode: Infima sets --ifm-button-color to the inverse font colour, near-black in
dark mode, precisely because the dark-mode accent is light. White on that accent
is 2.75:1. Infima's own value is 6.1:1. Both buttons now use Infima's classes
alone, with button--primary on the outline one so it has an accent border.

Base directory for this skill: D:\oh-my-posh\.claude\skills\code-changes

# Code Changes

The workflow for going from an issue, pull request, idea, or feature request to shipped code.
Follow the phases in order. Analysis always comes first; code comes last.

Each phase has a reference file with the full instructions. **Read the reference file when you
enter the phase** — not before, and never skip it because the phase "looks obvious".

## Roles

Assign work based on model capability. The coordinator is not the strongest model — it's the one
that stays resident, owns every phase by default, and knows when it's out of its depth.

| Role        | Capability tier                                               | Owns                                                                          |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Coordinator | Capable mid-tier, resident for the whole task                | Analysis, plan, delegation, supervision, verification, delivery — by default |
| Escalation  | Strongest reasoning model available; invoked only on trigger | The specific judgment call the coordinator flagged, then control returns     |
| Implementer | Same tier as coordinator, or smaller for trivial edits        | Executing one pinned, self-contained task                                    |

Concrete model names per vendor (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) and how to run the split in Claude
Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, or IDE agents: [references/model-tiers.md](references/model-tiers.md).

When the current agent already runs at implementer tier, there's no separate delegation step for
standard work: plan and execute directly, still following every phase. Escalate to the strongest
model only when a trigger fires — see [references/escalate.md](references/escalate.md) — never by
default and never for a routine judgment call the coordinator is equipped to make itself.

## The flow

1. **Analyze** ([references/analyze.md](references/analyze.md)) — root cause and scope,
   validated against the code, never against the report alone.
2. **Plan** ([references/plan.md](references/plan.md)) — pinned spec, task split, parallel vs
   sequential, workspace per task.
3. **Delegate** ([references/delegate.md](references/delegate.md)) — match each task to the
   right executor, coordinator-tier by default.
4. **Supervise** ([references/supervise.md](references/supervise.md)) — monitor, unblock, and
   critically review implementer output.
5. **Verify** ([references/verify.md](references/verify.md)) — quality gates plus functional
   proof, never delegated downward.
6. **Deliver** ([references/deliver.md](references/deliver.md)) — conventional commits and an
   outcome-first report.

Analyze, Supervise, and Verify each carry an escalation checkpoint — see
[references/escalate.md](references/escalate.md) — for handing one specific judgment call to the
strongest available model without giving up ownership of the phase.

**Stop gate:** Phase 1 ends with reporting the analysis and proposed approach to the user and
waiting for a go. Skip the gate only when the user already gave the go in the request itself
("do it", "fix it and commit", "implement with Sonnet").

## Special cases

These entry points replace or extend Phase 1; the rest of the flow applies unchanged.

- Pull request review comments →
  [references/pr-review-comments.md](references/pr-review-comments.md)
- Issue triage → [references/issue-triage.md](references/issue-triage.md)

content.text: ## Analysis ### Homepage — found the cause Direction A's hero was **left-aligned, gap `1.1rem`**, install box a single bordered unit, prompt on a dark rounded card, features as bordered cards: ```css .mock-a .m-hero { padding: 2.5rem 0 2.75rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1.1rem; } .mock-a .card { border: 1px solid var(--a-rule); border-radius: 9px; padding: 0.95rem 1rem; } .mock-a .termcard { background: var(--a-deep); border-radius: 9px; } ``` Phase 1 shipped `text-align: center`, `align-items: center`, `gap: 2rem`, no card, bare `` ([styles.module.css:8-76](website/src/pages/styles.module.css:8)). Centering deletes the shared left edge that held the stack together; doubling the gap turns five elements into five islands. That is the "white, small, white" bounce — nothing anchors the eye. Infima note: `col--4` carries padding gutters, so a border on `.feature` itself makes cards touch. Cards need an inner `div`. ### Segment catalog — three of the four proposed facets are not real I checked each against source rather than trusting the design doc: | Facet | Verdict | Evidence | |---|---|---| | Cacheable | **dead** — 117/117 | `Cache *Cache` is on the generic struct, [segment.go:44](src/config/segment.go:44). Doc's "61" was mockup filler | | Async | **dead** | top-level config flag, not per-segment | | Needs Nerd Font | **dead, wrong tier** | 0/117 segment docs and 2/110 Go segment files contain a PUA codepoint. Icons come from the *theme*. Belongs on the themes gallery | | Needs auth | **real, ~8** | `APIKey`/`AccessToken`/`RefreshToken` reads: brewfather, copilot, lastfm, nightscout, owm, strava, todoist, withings. True OAuth is 3 | | Group | **real, 8** | derivable from directory | Replacements that are true and actually discriminating: **group**, **needs a token or account**, **hits the network every prompt**, **platform-limited** (`winget`, `winreg` gate on GOOS). Free-text search stays the highest-value control regardless. ### Data source — better than expected `## What` is uniform across all 117 docs and its first paragraph is a usable one-liner. Title and path come from frontmatter and directory. So cards generate at build time — no 117-entry hand-authored file, only the two small curated flag lists, which a test can pin against the Go source. ### Out of scope Themes gallery, per-segment live previews (needs the Phase 2 renderer), FAQ split.

Counts reconcile: **118 registered types, 117 real segments.** `exit` is a legacy alias — `EXIT` and `STATUS` both construct `&segments.Status{}` ([segment_types.go:426,483](src/config/segment_types.go:426)). The other two mismatches are naming skew: type `go` ↔ doc `golang`, type `copilot_cli` ↔ doc `copilot-cli`.

That gives the catalog a drift guard: Go registry is the census, docs are the content, build fails if they disagree.

Two corrections to what I told you earlier:

- **Auth is 11, not 8**, in four tiers — hosted OAuth (strava, withings), `oh-my-posh auth` device flow (copilot, ytm), `api_key` option (lastfm, owm, todoist, brewfather), token-in-URL (nightscout, wakatime, http). I'd wrongly included nightscout via a comment match and missed ytm and http entirely.
- **`themes/schema.json` carries 99 segment blocks with descriptions and full per-option schema** — richer than anything I'd found. It covers 99 of 117 and its titles don't match the docs, so it's not the catalog spine, but it's a better long-term source than doc scraping.

Writing the plan.

# Phase 2a — Segment catalog + homepage rhythm Two independent workstreams. No renderer work; no Go changes. ## Verified facts this plan rests on | Fact | Evidence | | --- | --- | | 118 `SegmentType` constants, 118 registry entries, 117 doc files | `src/config/segment_types.go:156-391`, `:394-521`; `website/docs/segments/*/*.mdx` | | `exit` is a legacy alias for `status` — both build `&segments.Status{}` | `segment_types.go:426`, `:483` | | Doc id ≠ config type in two cases: `golang`→`go`, `copilot-cli`→`copilot_cli` | reconciliation script | | Frontmatter is exactly `id`, `title`, `sidebar_label` in all 117 | agent census | | `## What` present in 117/117, first paragraph is the description | agent census | | `Cache` is a field on the generic `Segment` struct — every segment is cacheable | `src/config/segment.go:44` | | Async is a top-level config flag, not per-segment | — | | Nerd Font glyphs live in themes, not segments: 0/117 docs and 2/110 Go files contain a PUA codepoint | scan | | 11 segments need credentials, in 4 tiers | see table below | | `useLocation` is the repo's only router hook usage; no `useHistory`, no `BrowserOnly` | `src/components/Auth.js:2` | | `classnames` is a direct dependency; React 19 | `website/package.json` | | No Docusaurus plugin in this repo uses `loadContent`/`setGlobalData` yet | `website/plugins/appinsights/index.js` | ### Facets that were in the design doc and are being dropped - **Cacheable** — would read 117/117. The mockup's "61" was filler. - **Async** — not a segment property. - **Needs Nerd Font** — not a segment property at all. Belongs on the themes gallery. Shipping it here would be a lie on 117 cards. Dropping these is deliberate and is the main deviation from the approved design. A facet that matches everything is not a filter; it is decoration that costs a click to discover. ### The credential tiers (curated, 11 entries) | Tier | Label | Segments | | --- | --- | --- | | `oauth` | Sign in via ohmyposh.dev | strava, withings | | `cli` | Run `oh-my-posh auth` | copilot, ytm | | `apikey` | API key in your config | lastfm, owm, todoist, brewfather | | `url` | Token inside the URL you supply | nightscout, wakatime, http | Authoritative for `cli`: `src/cli/auth.go:23-26` (`ValidArgs: copilot, ytmda`). Authoritative for `oauth`: `src/segments/strava.go:17`, `src/segments/withings.go:79` embed `http.OAuthRequest`. The other two tiers are doc-derived and hand-curated. --- ## Workstream 1 — the catalog ### Placement (decided) Standalone `/segments` page. Full width, no docs sidebar competing with the facet rail. `docs/segments/overview.mdx` keeps its grouped link list — it is the sidebar category target (`sidebars.js:63-68`) and `llms.txt` points at it — and gains a link across to `/segments`. ### Data contract — PINNED Both Task A and Task B build against this exact shape. Neither may change it. ```js // window[...].globalData['oh-my-posh-segments'].default { segments: [ { id: 'golang', // doc filename without extension; the URL slug type: 'go', // the string you put in your config `type` field name: 'Golang', // frontmatter `title` group: 'languages', // directory name groupLabel: 'Languages', // display label href: '/docs/segments/languages/golang', description: 'Display the currently active Golang version.', auth: null, // or 'oauth' | 'cli' | 'apikey' | 'url' }, // ... 117 entries, sorted by name within group ], groups: [ { id: 'cli', label: 'CLI', count: 39 }, // ... 8 entries, sorted by count descending ], authTiers: [ { id: 'oauth', label: 'Sign in via ohmyposh.dev', count: 2 }, { id: 'cli', label: 'Run oh-my-posh auth', count: 2 }, { id: 'apikey', label: 'API key in your config', count: 4 }, { id: 'url', label: 'Token in your URL', count: 3 }, ], } ``` `group` values are the eight directory names: `cli`, `cloud`, `health`, `languages`, `music`, `scm`, `system`, `web`. `groupLabel` for `scm` is `Source control`; the rest are the capitalised directory name except `CLI`. ### Task A — build-time data plugin **Owns, and creates:** `website/plugins/segments/index.js`, `website/plugins/segments/data.js`. Touches nothing else. Does **not** edit `docusaurus.config.js` — the coordinator wires it up. CommonJS, matching `website/plugins/appinsights/index.js`. Shape: ```js module.exports = function (context, options) { return { name: 'oh-my-posh-segments', async loadContent() { /* read + validate, return the object above */ }, async contentLoaded({ content, actions }) { actions.setGlobalData(content); }, }; }; ``` `loadContent` steps: 1. Walk `/website/docs/segments/*/` for `*.mdx`, skipping `overview.mdx`. Derive `group` from the directory, `id` from the filename. 2. Parse frontmatter for `title`. Do not add a YAML dependency — the frontmatter is three flat `key: value` lines in all 117 files; a line scan between the two `---` fences is correct and has no failure mode here. If a file's frontmatter lacks `title`, throw. 3. Extract the description: the first non-empty paragraph after the `## What` heading, joined onto one line. Then normalise: - `[text][ref]` and `[text](url)` → `text` - `` `code` `` → `code` - collapse runs of whitespace - if it does not end in `.`, `!` or `?`, leave it alone (do not invent punctuation) If `## What` is missing or its first paragraph is empty, throw naming the file. 4. Read `/src/config/segment_types.go`. Parse the constant block (`^\t([A-Z0-9_]+)\s+SegmentType = "([a-z0-9_-]+)"$`) and the registry map body that starts at `var Segments = map[SegmentType]func() SegmentWriter{` (`^\t([A-Z0-9_]+):`). Resolve map keys to type strings. 5. **Assert, throwing a message that names the offenders:** - every registry key resolves to a declared constant - every registered type has a doc file, after applying `TYPE_TO_DOC_ID` and skipping `IGNORED_TYPES` - every doc file maps back to a registered type - every key in the override maps corresponds to a known doc id A build must fail loudly when a segment is added to Go and not documented, or vice versa. That guard is the reason this is a plugin and not a committed JSON file. 6. Attach `auth` from `AUTH_TIERS`, `description` overrides from `DESCRIPTION_OVERRIDES`. 7. Compute `groups` and `authTiers` counts from the assembled list, never hardcode them. `website/plugins/segments/data.js` holds the curated tables and nothing else: ```js const TYPE_TO_DOC_ID = { go: 'golang', copilot_cli: 'copilot-cli' }; const IGNORED_TYPES = new Set(['exit']); // legacy alias for `status` const AUTH_TIERS = { strava: 'oauth', withings: 'oauth', copilot: 'cli', ytm: 'cli', lastfm: 'apikey', owm: 'apikey', todoist: 'apikey', brewfather: 'apikey', nightscout: 'url', wakatime: 'url', http: 'url' }; const AUTH_TIER_LABELS = { oauth: 'Sign in via ohmyposh.dev', cli: 'Run oh-my-posh auth', apikey: 'API key in your config', url: 'Token in your URL' }; const GROUP_LABELS = { cli: 'CLI', cloud: 'Cloud', health: 'Health', languages: 'Languages', music: 'Music', scm: 'Source control', system: 'System', web: 'Web' }; const DESCRIPTION_OVERRIDES = {}; // filled by the coordinator after reviewing the extraction ``` Every one of `IGNORED_TYPES`, `TYPE_TO_DOC_ID` and the tier assignments carries a comment saying why. A reader six months out must not have to re-derive that `exit` is an alias. **Deliverable beyond the code:** write the 117 extracted descriptions, one per line as `id\tdescription`, to `C:\Users\jande\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--oh-my-posh\6c0a282a-886f-458d-a426-93d95104b4a6\scratchpad\extracted-descriptions.tsv`. The coordinator reviews that and authors the overrides. Do not write overrides yourself. ### Task B — catalog component and page **Owns, and creates:** `website/src/components/SegmentCatalog/index.js`, `website/src/components/SegmentCatalog/styles.module.css`, `website/src/pages/segments.js`. Touches nothing else. Build against the pinned contract above. Read it with: ```js import { usePluginData } from '@docusaurus/useGlobalData'; const { segments, groups, authTiers } = usePluginData('oh-my-posh-segments'); ``` Layout — mirrors the approved mockup, retoned onto Infima tokens so it is theme-aware (the mockup was drawn in Direction B's fixed dark palette; do not hardcode those colours): - Two-column grid, `13.5rem 1fr`, collapsing to one column under 700px where the facet rail becomes a top strip with a bottom border instead of a right border. - **Facet rail** — one `
` per facet group, legend styled as the mockup's `.lbl` (monospace, `0.62rem`, `letter-spacing: 0.15em`, uppercase, muted). Real `` elements, visually restyled — do not fake them with spans, the mockup did that only because it was static artwork. Each row shows its count right-aligned in monospace with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. - **Counts are live**: each facet's count reflects what selecting it would yield given the *other* currently-active facets and the search term. A facet whose count is 0 stays visible but is disabled and dimmed — never removed, because a rail that reflows on every keystroke is unusable. - Within one facet group, checks are OR'd. Across groups, AND'd. - **Search** over `name`, `type`, `id` and `description`, case-insensitive, substring. **Do not bind ⌘K or Ctrl-K** — Algolia DocSearch already owns that chord sitewide. No global keyboard shortcut at all; a plain labelled input. - **Result grid** — `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(190px, 1fr))`, gap `0.7rem`. Each card is a `` to `href`, `border: 1px solid var(--ifm-color-emphasis-200)`, `border-radius: 8px`, `background: var(--ifm-background-surface-color)`, hover raises the border to the accent. Card contents, in order: the `type` string in monospace as the primary name; the description; a tag row. - **Tags**: the group label always; `needs auth` when `auth` is set, in the warning tone (`--ifm-color-warning-darkest` on light, lightest on dark) with `title` set to the tier label. Tags are ``, not links. - The `type` is the headline because it is the string a user types into their config. Where `type !== id`, that distinction is exactly the thing they need and cannot get from the sidebar today. Show `name` as secondary text on the card when it differs meaningfully. - A results count line above the grid: `117 segments` / `9 of 117 segments`. - An empty state when the filter matches nothing, with a button that clears all filters. **URL state:** ```js import { useHistory, useLocation } from '@docusaurus/router'; ``` - `?group=cli,cloud&auth=oauth&q=kube`. Omit any key that is empty. Never write `?` alone. - Read with `new URLSearchParams(useLocation().search)` — same idiom as `src/components/Auth.js:6`. - Write with `history.replace`, not `push`, so typing in the search box does not bury the back button under one entry per keystroke. - Initial state comes from the URL, so a shared link restores the view. - **SSR safety:** never touch `window` or `document` during render. On the server `useLocation().search` is `''`, which must render the full unfiltered list — that is also what makes the page indexable and what Algolia will crawl. No `BrowserOnly` wrapper; the whole page must server-render. `website/src/pages/segments.js` is a thin wrapper: `` containing a short header (`

Segments

` plus one sentence and a link to the configuration reference) and ``. Derive the count from the data; do not hardcode `117` in JSX. Match repo conventions: plain function declarations, `export default X;` at the bottom, `import React from 'react'`, CSS modules, `classnames` for conditional classes. ### Task D — the docs index **Owns:** `website/docs/segments/overview.mdx`. Touches nothing else. Keep the eight grouped lists exactly as they are — they are the sidebar's index and what `llms.txt` and the skill files point at. Change only the intro paragraph so it routes to the catalog first, in the house voice (plain, no marketing register, no exclamation): > A segment is a single piece of information in your prompt — the current path, a Git status, > a language version, a cloud context. See [Segment][segment] for how to configure one. > > To search and filter all 117 segments, use the [segment catalog](/segments). The full list > follows, grouped by category. Do not renumber, reorder or reword the lists themselves. ### Coordinator-owned `website/docusaurus.config.js` — add `'./plugins/segments'` to `plugins`, retarget the navbar `Segments` item from `docs/segments/overview` to `/segments`. Two edits, no delegation, so no task contends for this file. --- ## Workstream 2 — homepage rhythm ### Task C **Owns:** `website/src/pages/index.js`, `website/src/pages/styles.module.css`. Touches nothing else. The complaint is real and the cause is specific: Direction A's hero was **left-aligned with a `1.1rem` gap**. What shipped is centred with a `2rem` gap. Centring removes the shared left edge that gave the stack a spine; doubling the gap turns five elements into five islands with nothing to hold them. Reference, from the approved mockup: ```css .mock-a .m-hero { padding: 2.5rem 0 2.75rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1.1rem; } .mock-a .card { border: 1px solid var(--a-rule); border-radius: 9px; padding: 0.95rem 1rem; } .mock-a .termcard { background: var(--a-deep); border-radius: 9px; margin-top: 0.5rem; } ``` Changes: 1. **Left-align the hero.** Drop `text-align: center` from `.heroBanner`; set `align-items: flex-start` on `.heroBanner :global(.container)`; drop the centring from `.installNote`; `.buttons` gets `justify-content: flex-start`. Two structural changes fall out of the review, both worth flagging before I proceed:

**The guard was going to run nowhere.** `code.yml` carries `paths-ignore: ['website/**']` and `docs.yml` only fires on push to `main`. A Go PR adding a segment would never have run the website build, so the drift check would have failed later, on someone else's deploy. And `docusaurus build` executes inside the Azure SWA action with `app_location: /website` — the repo already works around that boundary twice by copying files in.

So the guard moves to Go: a test in `src/config/` that calls `Template()` on every registered writer, asserts registry↔docs 1:1, and asserts a committed `registry.json` matches. That runs on every Go PR, gives exact Nerd Font detection with no regex, and removes the cross-boundary read.

# Phase 2a — Segment catalog + homepage rhythm Two workstreams. No renderer work. One small Go addition (a test plus a generated JSON), for reasons given under "Where the guard lives". Revised after review. Every change from the first draft is marked **[R]** with the reason. ## Verified facts this plan rests on | Fact | Evidence | | --- | --- | | 118 `SegmentType` constants, 118 registry entries, 117 doc files | `src/config/segment_types.go:156-391`, `:394-521` | | `exit` is a legacy alias for `status` — both build `&segments.Status{}` | `segment_types.go:426`, `:483` | | Doc id ≠ config type in exactly two cases: `golang`→`go`, `copilot-cli`→`copilot_cli` | reconciliation script | | Frontmatter is exactly `id`, `title`, `sidebar_label` in all 117; filename always equals `id` | census | | `## What` present in 117/117 | census | | `Cache` is a field on the generic `Segment` struct — every segment is cacheable | `src/config/segment.go:44` | | Async is a top-level config flag, not per-segment | — | | **28 of 117 segments use a Nerd Font glyph in their default `Template()`** **[R]** | scan of `Template()` bodies incl. `\uXXXX` escapes | | 11 segments need credentials, in 4 tiers | table below | | `@docusaurus/router` exports `useHistory`; `usePluginData(name)` with no id is correct | `core/lib/client/exports/router.js:7`, `useGlobalData.js:21` | | Docusaurus SSR renders `` — **no query string** | `core/lib/client/serverEntry.js:27` | | `--ifm-background-surface-color` is `#fff` in light — identical to the page canvas | `infima/dist/css/default/default.css:135` → `:105` | | `hero.png` is opaque, 1100×44, background `#173448` | pixel scan | ### **[R]** Correction to the first draft The first draft asserted "0/117 docs and 2/110 Go files contain a PUA codepoint" and dropped the Nerd Font facet as fictional. That scan searched only for **literal** PUA characters and missed the `\uXXXX` escape form, which is how this repo writes glyphs almost everywhere. The real numbers are 112/117 docs and 41/110 Go files. The facet is restored, but scoped to the only definition that is both true and useful: > **Needs a Nerd Font** = the segment's default `Template()` contains a codepoint in the > Private Use Area. 28/117. That is discriminating, it is exactly checkable, and it answers a real question ("what can I use on a terminal that cannot do Nerd Fonts?"). It is *not* a claim about themes, which override templates and overwhelmingly do require a Nerd Font. ### Facets still being dropped, and why - **Cacheable** — would read 117/117. `Cache` is on the generic struct. The mockup's "61" was filler. - **Async** — a top-level config flag, not a segment property. A facet that matches everything is not a filter. ### The credential tiers (curated, 11 entries) | Tier | Label | Segments | | --- | --- | --- | | `oauth` | Sign in via ohmyposh.dev | strava, withings | | `cli` | Run `oh-my-posh auth` | copilot, ytm | | `apikey` | API key in your config | lastfm, owm, todoist, brewfather | | `url` | Token in your URL | nightscout, wakatime, http | Authoritative for `cli`: `src/cli/auth.go:23-26` (`ValidArgs: copilot, ytmda`). Authoritative for `oauth`: `src/segments/strava.go:17`, `src/segments/withings.go:79` embed `http.OAuthRequest`. The other two tiers are doc-derived and hand-curated. Review confirmed independently that there is no twelfth segment needing credentials. **[R]** The tier labels above are the single source. Use these strings verbatim; the first draft carried two different wordings for the `url` tier. --- ## Where the guard lives **[R]** The first draft put the doc↔registry drift check in the Docusaurus plugin. That was wrong on two counts: 1. **It would never run on a pull request.** `.github/workflows/code.yml:3-9` and `build_code.yml:3-9` both carry `paths-ignore: ['website/**']`, and `.github/workflows/docs.yml:4-9` triggers only on push to `main`. A Go-only PR adding a `SegmentType` would never build the website. The failure would land on `main` and break an unrelated deploy. 2. **It reads across a boundary the repo already respects.** `docusaurus build` runs inside `Azure/static-web-apps-deploy` with `app_location: "/website"` (`docs.yml:47-58`). The repo works around this twice already — `npm run themes` runs as a separate runner step (`docs.yml:35-41`) and `themes/schema.json` is copied into `website/api/data/` (`docs.yml:42-46`). Reading `../src/config/segment_types.go` at build time breaks that contract for no gain. So the guard becomes a **Go test**, and the website consumes a committed JSON. --- ## Task E — the Go guard and the registry artifact **[R]** **Owns, and creates:** `src/config/segment_catalog_test.go`, `website/plugins/segments/registry.json`. Touches nothing else. Go only — no website code. The test builds the truth from the live registry and compares it to the committed JSON. 1. Iterate `config.Segments`. For each `SegmentType` key: - Skip `EXIT` — it is a legacy alias for `STATUS`; both construct `&segments.Status{}`. Name the reason in a comment. - Construct the writer via the map's factory and call `Template()`. - `needsNerdFont` is true when any rune in that string falls in `U+E000..U+F8FF` or `U+F0000..U+FFFFD`. - Recover from a panic in `Template()` and fail the test naming the segment. Do not let one bad writer take down the suite with an unattributed stack trace. 2. Walk `../../website/docs/segments/*/` for `*.mdx`, skipping `overview.mdx`. Assert: - every registered type has a doc, after applying the alias map `{go: golang, copilot_cli: "copilot-cli"}` - every doc maps back to a registered type Failure messages must name the offending segments — "counts differ" is not actionable. 3. Marshal to `website/plugins/segments/registry.json`, sorted by type for a stable diff: ```json [ { "type": "angular", "docId": "angular", "needsNerdFont": false }, { "type": "go", "docId": "golang", "needsNerdFont": false } ] ``` 4. Compare against the committed file. On mismatch, fail with a diff **and write the corrected JSON to the path**, so the fix is `go test ./config/... && git add`. A guard that tells you only that you are wrong costs more than one that hands you the answer. Expect 117 entries, 28 with `needsNerdFont: true`. Treat a different count as a signal to stop and report, not to adjust the expectation. --- ## Workstream 1 — the catalog ### Placement (decided) Standalone `/segments`. Full width, no docs sidebar competing with the facet rail. `docs/segments/overview.mdx` keeps its grouped link list — it is the sidebar category target (`sidebars.js:63-68`) and `llms.txt` points at it — and gains a link across. ### Data contract — PINNED Tasks A and B build against this exact shape. ```js // usePluginData('oh-my-posh-segments') { segments: [ { id: 'golang', // doc filename without extension; the URL slug type: 'go', // the string you put in your config `type` field name: 'Golang', // frontmatter `title` group: 'languages', groupLabel: 'Languages', href: '/docs/segments/languages/golang', description: 'Display the currently active Golang version.', auth: null, // or 'oauth' | 'cli' | 'apikey' | 'url' needsNerdFont: false, }, // ... 117 entries, sorted by name within group ], groups: [{ id: 'cli', label: 'CLI', count: 39 }], // 8, sorted by count desc authTiers: [{ id: 'oauth', label: 'Sign in via ohmyposh.dev', count: 2 }], // 4, fixed order total: 117, } ``` Groups are the eight directory names. `groupLabel` for `scm` is `Source control`, `cli` is `CLI`, the rest are the capitalised directory name. ### Task A — build-time data plugin **Owns, and creates:** `website/plugins/segments/index.js`, `website/plugins/segments/data.js`. Does **not** edit `docusaurus.config.js`, and does **not** create `registry.json` — Task E owns that file. **[R] Handoff:** Task A creates `data.js` with `DESCRIPTION_OVERRIDES = {}` and then releases the file. The coordinator is the second and final writer of that constant. No other task touches it. CommonJS, matching `website/plugins/appinsights/index.js`. `website/package.json` has no `"type": "module"`, so a CJS plugin loads fine under the ESM config. ```js module.exports = function (context, options) { return { name: 'oh-my-posh-segments', async loadContent() { /* returns the object above */ }, async contentLoaded({ content, actions }) { actions.setGlobalData(content); }, }; }; ``` `loadContent` steps: 1. Four agents running. Where things stand:

**Review caught six defects worth having.** The two that would have shipped broken:

1. **My Nerd Font scan was wrong.** I searched for literal PUA characters; this repo writes glyphs as `\uXXXX` escapes. Real count is 112/117 docs, and 28/117 segments need one in their default `Template()`. I'd told you the facet was fictional and dropped it. It's restored — and now derived exactly rather than curated, by calling `Template()` on each registered writer in a Go test.

2. **Hydration.** Docusaurus SSRs `<StaticRouter location={pathname}>` — pathname only, no query. Initialising filter state from `useLocation().search` means `/segments?group=cli` renders 39 cards on the client against 117 in the server HTML, and React 19 throws the whole server tree away. My "don't touch `window`" instruction wouldn't have helped, because `useLocation()` is the leak. Fixed with `useIsBrowser()`.

Also fixed: card fill was `--ifm-background-surface-color`, which is `#fff` in light mode — border with no fill; the auth tag colour was 3.44:1, below AA; the description extractor would have silently shipped a WSL caution notice as `battery`'s description; and the termcard background didn't match `hero.png`'s actual baked-in `#173448`.

**One structural change I made on the review's evidence, worth your eye:** the drift guard moved from the website build into a Go test. `code.yml` carries `paths-ignore: ['website/**']` and `docs.yml` only runs on push to `main`, so a website-side guard would never have fired on a Go PR — it'd have broken a later deploy instead. The Go test also gives exact Nerd Font detection with no Go-source regex parsing, and drops the cross-boundary file read that `docusaurus build` couldn't reliably do inside the Azure SWA action.

That adds `src/config/segment_catalog_test.go` and a committed `website/plugins/segments/registry.json` to what was meant to be a website-only phase. Say the word if you'd rather keep Go untouched and accept a weaker guard.

`/segments` lands standalone; the docs index and the navbar retarget land after it, since `onBrokenLinks: 'throw'` fails any build that links a route that doesn't exist yet.

test(config): assert the segment registry matches the docs

Adding a segment means touching the registry, the docs and the sidebar by
hand, and nothing checked that those stayed in agreement. A segment could be
registered with no documentation, or documented after being removed, and the
first sign would be a reader hitting a page that no longer describes anything.

Derive the catalog from the live registry instead: call Template() on every
registered writer to find which segments need a Nerd Font glyph, then assert
a bidirectional match against the doc files. The result is written to
website/plugins/segments/registry.json, which the website consumes.

The test lives here rather than in the website build because the website is
not built on pull requests: code.yml ignores website/**, and docs.yml only
runs on push to main. A guard in the Docusaurus build would have caught drift
one deploy too late, and blamed whoever pushed next.

On mismatch the test rewrites the JSON as well as failing, so the fix is to
rerun it and stage the result rather than hand-edit a generated file.

EOF

**The catalog.** Search, category facet, setup facet, Nerd Font facet — all with live counts that respond to the other active filters. Filter state in the URL. Your config is close to a worst case for this work, which makes it a good acceptance test:

- **`rprompt`** — a right-aligned block, which needs terminal width to position. SVG has no terminal, so width becomes an explicit parameter rather than an ambient fact.
- **`shell_integration` + `iterm_features`** — these emit OSC 133/1337 sequences that are *not visual*. An SVG encoder must drop them, and today they're interleaved into the same byte stream as the colors.
- 3 styles (diamond, plain, powerline), 5 `background_templates`, 8 leading diamonds, a palette, `min_width`.

That already argues where the seam goes: below template resolution, above escape emission, so non-visual escapes never enter the run stream at all.

Checking whether byte-identical verification is even achievable before I plan around it.

content.text:
That comparison is confounded — the recorded data came from *my* machine (real git state, real path), so "more text" doesn't prove the bug. Discarding it as evidence.

Here's where the analysis lands.

## Phase 2 analysis

### The safety net works — but not the way I described it

Naive golden files fail: **46 of 122 themes are non-deterministic**. Cause is `website/segment_data.json`, which pins 24 of 117 segments; everything else runs live against the clock and filesystem.

Recording per-theme with `config export data` first gives **122/122 deterministic**, verified twice. That's the harness.

### A real bug in `--data`, and this phase depends on it

`restoreData` returns at [segment.go:203](src/config/segment.go:203), *before* `segment.writer.Enabled()` at `:243`. But `Time.Format` is computed inside `Enabled()` ([time.go:27](src/segments/time.go:27)). So pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` makes the segment render empty — and its entire rprompt block silently vanishes, 419 bytes → 328. Adding `Format` restores it.

**14 of the 24 segments pinned in `website/segment_data.json` assign derived state inside `Enabled()`** (aws 9, strava 7, git 6, battery 5, gcp 4…). A hand-written data file must reproduce all of it exactly, with no validation and silent failure.

The recorder gets this right because it captures post-`Enabled()` state. So: hand-written data files are unsound, and `website/segment_data.json` is hand-written. I have **not** demonstrated a currently-visible defect on the site — my attempt to measure that was confounded by environment, and I'm not going to claim it.

### The seam is not where I told you it was

I said "extract a run stream between resolver and encoder in `terminal/`". That doesn't work as stated:

- **Semantic colour is destroyed at [writer.go:377](src/terminal/writer.go:377)**, before anything is written. `asAnsiColors` collapses `#FF5733`, `p:accent`, `parentBackground` and gradients into an SGR payload string like `"48;2;255;87;51"`. Gradient stops and the Apple Terminal 256-colour downgrade are gone irreversibly.
- **Segment identity doesn't exist in `terminal` at all.** `Write` is called once per *fragment* — leading diamond, text, separator, trailing diamond are four separate calls from `prompt/engine.go`. Block boundaries are implied only by `String()`.

So `data-segment`/`data-block` attributes can't come from a `terminal`-only run stream. Capture has to straddle `prompt/engine.go` for structure, or colour resolution has to move later.

### The refactor has a better justification than SVG

There are **three independent copies of the same tokenizer** — `writeBody:484`, `writeBodyGradient:543`, `countVisibleCells:894` — which [writer.go:886-892](src/terminal/writer.go:886) documents must stay in lockstep by hand. That's worth fixing on its own merits.

Two latent bugs found in passing: `isHyperlink` is never reset anywhere, so one unbalanced `<LINK>` corrupts every subsequent `Write` for the process lifetime; and OSC 8 emission has no `Plain` guard, so `--plain` still emits hyperlink escapes.

### The deletion is ~20x what I estimated

I said ≈1,500 lines and 3 dependencies. Actual: 1,877 first-party + ~27,700 third-party = **~29,600 lines**, 4 modules (`gg`, `stackblur`, `x/image`, `freetype`), verified exclusive by `go list -deps` set difference. The no-build-tag conclusion holds much more strongly than I argued.

### The current imager is worse than "re-parses ANSI"

Map iteration over prefix-overlapping regexes means **the same input can parse differently between runs**. 256-colour `\x1b[38;5;Nm` isn't handled at all — those bytes get drawn as visible glyphs. Bold and italic can't coexist. Strikethrough is parsed and discarded. Hyperlink URLs are dropped. And a font-download failure **exits 0 with no image**, so a CI run without network silently publishes nothing.

### Benchmark gate: allocations, not time

ns/op swings 8x run-to-run on this box (1492–11816 for one benchmark); B/op and allocs/op are exactly stable. Baseline captured: `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` 9,150 B / 95 allocs, `BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 602 B / 14 allocs.

## What I'd change about the plan

Split what was one phase into three, because the first part is independently valuable and shippable:

| | |
|---|---|
| **2.0** | Golden harness over 122 themes from recorded data; fix or hard-fail the `Enabled()`-bypass in `restoreData`; regenerate `segment_data.json` via the recorder |
| **2.1** | Collapse the three tokenizers into one; de-globalize enough to make capture possible. This is the actual risk, and it's justified without SVG |
| **2.2** | Run stream + SVG encoder + `--format svg` |

input.content:
# Phase 2.0 — Deterministic replay and the golden harness

The safety net for the renderer work, plus the correctness bug found while building it.
No run stream, no SVG, no changes to `terminal/`.

## Verified facts this plan rests on

| Fact | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `restoreData` returns before `writer.Enabled()` is ever called | `src/config/segment.go:203-205` vs `:243` |
| `Time.Format` is computed inside `Enabled()`, so replay renders it empty | `src/segments/time.go:27-28` |
| Pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` silently drops the whole rprompt block | measured: 419 → 328 bytes on `themes/agnosterplus.omp.json` |
| Adding `Format` to the pinned data restores it exactly | measured: 419 bytes, renders `10:41:00` |
| 53 of 102 `Enabled()` implementations assign template-visible state | scan of receiver-field assignments |
| At least 24 of those perform direct I/O (`RunCommand`, `HasFiles`, `HTTPRequest`, …) | scan; more do so transitively |
| `website/segment_data.json` pins 24 of 117 segments; the rest run live | `src/config/segment.go:487-507` (`DataKey`) |
| With that hand-written file, 46 of 122 themes render non-deterministically | two full sweeps, diffed |
| With per-theme `config export data` recordings, 122 of 122 are deterministic | two full sweeps, diffed |
| The recorder captures post-`Enabled()` state, including `Format` | `tokyo.json` and friends contain every derived field |
| Recorded fixtures are ~580 KB; goldens ~237 KB | `du` over 122 files each |
| **Every recorded fixture contains the recording machine's real username** | 122/122 contain `jande` |
| **No theme PNG is tracked in git** — they are generated in CI only | `git ls-files 'website/static/img/themes/*'` returns 0 |
| ns/op varies ~8x run to run on this hardware; B/op and allocs/op are exactly stable | `-count=3` baseline |

Baseline to hold: `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` 9,150 B / 95 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 602 B / 14 allocs;
`BenchmarkWritePlainASCII` 280 B / 6 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteSolid` 465 B / 16 allocs;
`BenchmarkWriteGradient` 1,762 B / 17 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteGradientChained` 789 B / 27 allocs.

## Decisions already taken

- Ship Phase 2.0 on its own, before the tokenizer refactor.
- **Hermetic by default, derive by opt-in.** Replay never calls `Enabled()` unless explicitly
  asked. This is what keeps the golden harness deterministic and keeps a future render endpoint
  free of live segment execution — the `http`, `owm`, `nba`, `ipify`, `todoist` and `wakatime`
  segments all take a URL or key from config, so any path that runs them server-side is an SSRF
  proxy.

## Deliberately out of scope

The run stream, the SVG encoder, the tokenizer collapse, deleting `cli/image/`, and the
missing `Plain` guard on OSC 8 hyperlink emission (it changes ANSI output, so it must land
after the harness exists, not with it).

---

## Task A — the replay contract

**Owns:** `src/config/data.go`, `src/config/segment.go`, `src/cli/data.go`,
`src/cli/config_export_data.go`, and their tests.

Three changes, in this order.

### A1. Mark recorded files

The recorder writes a provenance marker into the file it produces. A top-level field on the
`Data` struct — a schema version is better than a bare boolean because it gives the next change
somewhere to go:

```json
{ "version": 1, "env": { … }, "segments": { … } }
```

Absent field means "hand-written", which is the current state of every existing file.

### A2. Fail loudly on unmarked data

On load, a file without the marker is a hard error naming the two ways forward:

> `<path>` was not produced by `oh-my-posh config export data`. Hand-written data files skip
> the segment's `Enabled()` step, so any field it derives will be missing and the segment can
> render empty. Record the file with `oh-my-posh config export data --config <config>
> --output <path>`, or pass `--data-derive` to compute derived state at render time.

The error must say *why*, not just *what*. The failure this replaces is silent and looks like
a theme bug.

### A3. `--data-derive`

An opt-in flag on the commands that accept `--data` (`print`, `config export image`). When set,
`restoreData` calls `segment.writer.Enabled()` first and unmarshals the pinned data **over** the
result, so derived fields are computed and pinned fields still win.

Order matters and is the whole point: `Enabled()` then overlay. The reverse recomputes over the
pinned values and discards them.

Document on the flag, in one line, that this re-runs live segment probes and is therefore
neither hermetic nor deterministic — it exists so a hand-written file stays usable locally.

**Verification:** `themes/agnosterplus.omp.json` with a data file containing only
`{"time":{"CurrentDate":"2026-01-01T09:41:00Z"}}` renders the time segment under
`--data-derive` and errors without it. Confirm the recorded-fixture path never calls `Enabled()`
— assert it, do not assume it, because that assertion is what the SSRF argument rests on.

---

## Task B — sanitized fixtures and the golden harness

**Owns:** a fixture-generation command or script, `src/prompt/golden_test.go` (or wherever
Task B judges correct after reading the existing test layout), and the committed fixtures.

### B1. Sanitize on record

**Recorded data cannot be committed as-is.** All 122 fixtures I generated contain my real
username, and the `env` block carries `UserName`, `HostName`, `PWD`, `AbsolutePWD`, `PSWD` and
`Folder`. Segment data embeds real paths too — `tokyo.json` contains a rendered template string
with the username in it, so scrubbing the `env` block alone is not enough.

Sanitization must therefore be a string-level pass over the whole serialized file, replacing the
recording machine's identity with fixed synthetic values, then the `env` block overwritten with:

```
UserName  alice
HostName  contoso-devbox
PWD       ~/dev/oh-my-posh
```

matching the values `website/segment_data.json` already uses, so the fixtures and the website
tell the same story.

**A test must assert no fixture contains the current user's name, hostname, or home path.**
Without it this regresses the first time someone regenerates on their own machine, and it
regresses silently into a public repo.

### B2. The harness

For each of the 122 bundled themes: render `print primary` with the sanitized fixture and
compare byte-for-byte against a committed golden.

- Fixtures ~580 KB, goldens ~237 KB. Acceptable; do not compress, a readable diff is the point.
- Failure output must show the first differing byte offset and a decoded escape context window.
  A diff of two ANSI blobs is unreadable otherwise, and this harness exists to be read during
  a refactor.
- Regeneration must be one documented command, and the test must name it on failure.
- The golden is the *current* output. This phase changes no rendering. If generating goldens
  produces a diff against what the current binary emits, stop and report — that is a bug found,
  not a golden to bless.

Wire into the workflow that runs on Go pull requests. Note `.github/workflows/code.yml` carries
`paths-ignore: ['website/**']`, which is fine here since everything lands under `src/`.

---

## Task C — make the website's data file valid

**Owns:** `website/segment_data.json`, `website/export_themes.mjs`, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`
if needed.

`website/segment_data.json` is hand-written and deliberately synthetic — it exists to make theme
screenshots look like a plausible machine, not to reflect any real one. Under A2 it now fails to
load.

Determine which of the two applies and implement it, reporting which and why:

1. **Preferred — make it a valid recorded file.** Record it, sanitize it to the same synthetic
   identity, and keep the curated values (`anycompany-prod`, `Contoso Production`, the pinned
   battery percentage) by overlaying them onto the recording. Keeps the website pipeline
   hermetic.
2. **Fallback — pass `--data-derive` from `export_themes.mjs`.** Honest and small, but the
   website images then depend on live segment probes on the CI runner. That is already true
   today for the 93 unpinned segments, so it is not a regression — but it is not an improvement
   either, and the theme images stay non-deterministic.

Do not silently pick the fallback because it is easier. If option 1 turns out to be
impractical, say what blocked it.

---

## Task D — reset `isHyperlink`

**Owns:** `src/terminal/writer.go` and its tests. Separate commit; unrelated to the rest.

`isHyperlink` is set at `writer.go:460`, `:503`, `:562` and cleared only by encountering
`<TEXT>`. It is not reset in `Write`'s prologue (`:385-392`) nor in `String()`'s deferred
cleanup (`:605-619`) — the only two reset points in the package. An unbalanced `<LINK>` with no
`</TEXT>` therefore leaves it `true` for the lifetime of the process, and every subsequent
`Write` takes the branch at `:700-703`: runes go straight into the builder with no length
counting and no shell escaping.

Reset it alongside the other per-render flags. Add a test that writes an unbalanced `<LINK>`
and asserts the next `Write` counts length correctly.

This must not change output for any balanced input — the golden harness from Task B is the
proof, so land it after B.

---

## Landing order

`A` → `B` → `C`, sequential: B's fixtures are invalid until A defines the marker, and C cannot
be validated until A2 is enforcing. `D` is independent but lands after B so the harness can
prove it inert.

## Verification (coordinator, not delegated)

1. `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` clean from `src/`.
2. All 122 goldens pass. Then deliberately corrupt one fixture and confirm the failure output
   names the theme and shows a readable escape context.
3. Re-run the full render sweep twice and diff — 122/122 identical, as measured today.
4. A data file lacking the marker fails with the explanatory error; the same file under
   `--data-derive` renders.
5. Assert the hermetic path does not call `Enabled()`. This is the SSRF-relevant claim.
6. Grep every committed fixture for the current user, host and home path — zero hits.
7. Benchmarks against the baseline above: allocs/op and B/op unchanged. Ignore ns/op, which
   swings 8x on this hardware.
8. `npm run themes` equivalent still produces images for a sample of themes.

8. **Anything else** that breaks the build, ships something wrong, or makes the harness give false confidence.

content.text:
Verified. My plan was built on a false premise, and I need to say so plainly.

## The review killed my plan. Three of the findings are mine to own.

**`--data` replay is not hermetic, and my 122/122 determinism was an artifact.**

The recorder skips disabled segments — [`if !segment.Enabled { continue }`](src/cli/config_export_data.go:129). So a fixture only covers what happened to be live on the recording machine, and everything else falls through to live execution:

| theme | configured | recorded | replay |
|---|---|---|---|
| tokyo | 16 | 9 | 0.08s |
| atomic | 24 | 9 | 0.08s |
| **chips** | 15 | 5 | **1.22s** |

That 1.22s is `wakatime` making a real HTTP call on the supposedly hermetic path. My determinism sweep passed only because the fixture's `PWD` doesn't exist, so every filesystem probe failed identically — change that path and it collapses. The SSRF constraint I carried into this phase from the start rests on the same false premise.

**Two more of mine:** there are **124** themes, not 122 — I globbed `*.omp.json` and missed two YAML themes, which go through a different unmarshal path and would have had zero coverage. And my citation of `DataKey` pointed at `restoreData`'s line range.

## Three that would have failed in CI

- **Timezone.** 65 themes carry a `time` segment, and `date` renders in the *renderer's* local zone. I demonstrated this myself without noticing: I pinned `09:41:00Z` and it rendered `10:41:00`. CI runners are UTC; my goldens would fail on every one.
- **`TERM_PROGRAM`.** [`color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`](src/terminal/writer.go:192) gates truecolor vs 256-colour emission. Same theme, same fixture, different bytes under macOS Terminal.app — and `code.yml` runs tests on all three OSes.
- **`prompt.New` reads the session cache** ([gob.go:44](src/config/gob.go:44)), so a harness looping over themes gets whatever config is cached, or the developer's own if `POSH_SESSION_ID` is set — which it is inside any real omp shell.

## And one design error

My A2 — hard-fail on unmarked data files — is a **breaking change to a feature shipped in v29.35.3**. [`data.mdx:54`](website/docs/configuration/data.mdx:54) explicitly teaches the opposite: *"A key left out falls back to the real environment, so specify only the properties your config depends on."* My plan had no docs task and would have broken every user following that page.

Also: Task C option 1 is circular, as the review put it — reproducing `segment_data.json` by recording would need a machine with AWS, Azure, GCP, kubectl, Terraform, Strava and Spotify all simultaneously authenticated. That's *why* it's hand-written.

## What this means for the phase

The centrepiece isn't the harness any more — it's the recorder. Record every segment with an explicit enabled flag, and make `restoreData` suppress recorded-but-disabled segments so they never probe. Only then is replay hermetic, only then is the harness meaningful, and only then does the render endpoint have a safety story.

That's a bigger, more invasive change than "build a safety net," and it lands in the same `Execute` path the tokenizer refactor will touch.
