# Phase 2.0 — Hermetic replay and the golden harness

The safety net for the renderer work, plus the correctness bug found while building it.
No run stream, no SVG, no tokenizer changes.

**Revision 2.** The first draft rested on a false premise: that `--data` replay is hermetic.
It is not. Every change from that draft is marked **[R]**.

## The premise that was wrong

`config export data` skips segments that were not enabled on the recording machine —
`src/cli/config_export_data.go:129-131`:

```go
for _, segment := range block.Segments {
    if !segment.Enabled {
        continue
    }
```

So a fixture covers only what happened to be live when it was recorded, and every other segment
falls through `restoreData` (`src/config/segment.go:488-491`, returns `false`) into the live
`segment.writer.Enabled()` at `:243`.

| theme | segments configured | recorded | replay |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tokyo | 16 | 9 | 0.08s |
| atomic | 24 | 9 | 0.08s |
| jandedobbeleer | 17 | 8 | 0.07s |
| **chips** | 15 | 5 | **1.22s** |

The 1.22s is `wakatime` making a live HTTP request during what was supposed to be a replay.

The earlier "122/122 deterministic" measurement was an artifact: the fixture's `PWD` does not
exist, so every filesystem probe failed identically on both sweeps. It proves nothing.

## Verified facts

| Fact | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `restoreData` returns before `writer.Enabled()` | `src/config/segment.go:203-205` vs `:243` |
| `Time.Format` is computed inside `Enabled()`, so replay renders it empty | `src/segments/time.go:27-28` |
| Pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` drops the whole rprompt block, silently | measured 419 → 328 bytes on `agnosterplus` |
| Adding `Format` restores it | measured 419 bytes, renders `10:41:00` |
| 53 of 102 `Enabled()` implementations assign template-visible state; ≥24 do I/O | scan |
| **The recorder skips disabled segments** | `src/cli/config_export_data.go:129-131` |
| **124 themes, not 122** — 122 `.omp.json` plus 2 `.omp.yaml` | `ls themes/*.omp.*` |
| **65 themes carry a `time` segment** | `grep -l '"type": *"time"'` |
| **`date` renders in the renderer's local zone** | pinned `09:41:00Z` rendered `10:41:00` here |
| **`color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`** gates truecolor vs 256-colour | `src/terminal/writer.go:192`, read at `src/color/colors.go:312` |
| **`prompt.New` returns the session-cached config, ignoring the path** | `src/config/gob.go:44-49`, called from `src/prompt/engine.go:804-806` |
| **`--data` shipped in v29.35.3 and `data.mdx` documents partial hand-written files** | `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx:54-55` |
| **No bundled theme uses `<LINK>`** | `grep -l '<LINK>' themes/*.omp.*` returns 0 |
| `isHyperlink` is reset in neither `Write`'s prologue nor `String()`'s cleanup | `writer.go:78`, `:385-392`, `:605-619` |
| `DataKey` is the segment `Alias` or `Type` | `src/config/segment.go:412-418` |
| No theme PNG is tracked in git | `git ls-files 'website/static/img/themes/*'` → 0 |
| ns/op swings ~8x on this hardware; B/op and allocs/op are exactly stable | `-count=3` |
| `LoadData` reads only `env` and `segments`, tolerating unknown top-level keys | `src/config/data.go:43-90` |

Baseline to hold: `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` 9,150 B / 95 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 602 B /
14 allocs; `BenchmarkWritePlainASCII` 280 B / 6 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteSolid` 465 B / 16 allocs;
`BenchmarkWriteGradient` 1,762 B / 17 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteGradientChained` 789 B / 27 allocs.

## Decisions taken

- Ship Phase 2.0 alone, before the tokenizer refactor.
- **[R] Fix the recorder properly.** Record every configured segment with an explicit enabled
  flag; `restoreData` suppresses recorded-but-disabled segments without probing. Hermeticity has
  to be real before the harness or any render endpoint can lean on it.
- **[R] No breaking change.** Hand-written partial files keep working, with a warning and
  correctly derived state. `data.mdx:54` documents them and `--data` shipped in v29.35.3.

## Out of scope

The run stream, the SVG encoder, the tokenizer collapse, deleting `cli/image/`, the missing
`Plain` guard on OSC 8 emission, recording tooltip segments (`buildDataDocument` iterates
`cfg.Blocks` only, `config_export_data.go:127`), and changing the `DataKey` scheme.

**[R] Known limitation to document, not fix:** themes with two segments of the same type and no
`alias` collide on `DataKey` — the recorder already warns `multiple segments share the data key
"text"; the last one wins`. Goldens will encode that lossy behaviour. That is acceptable: the
harness is a change-detector, and the behaviour it locks in is the current one.

---

## Task A — make replay hermetic

**Owns:** `src/cli/config_export_data.go`, `src/config/data.go`, `src/config/segment.go`,
`src/cli/data.go`, `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx`, and their tests.

### A1. Record everything

Drop the `!segment.Enabled` skip. Record every configured segment, carrying its enabled state:

```json
{ "version": 1, "env": { … }, "segments": { "git": { "enabled": true, "data": { … } } } }
```

Shape is Task A's call, but the enabled flag must be per segment and must survive round-trip.
Keep backward compatibility with the current flat shape, since `website/segment_data.json` and
every user file use it.

`version` is safe to add: `LoadData` decodes the root into `map[string]json.RawMessage` and
reads only `env` and `segments`, so unknown top-level keys are already tolerated on the JSON,
YAML and TOML paths.

### A2. Suppress recorded-but-disabled segments

In `restoreData`:

- present and enabled → current behaviour: unmarshal the pinned data, `Enabled = true`, return
  `true`. No probe.
- **[R]** present and disabled → `Enabled = false`, `restored = true`, return `true`. **No
  probe.** This is the case that makes replay hermetic.
- absent → return `false` and fall through, as today.

**[R]** Do not move the recorded path's short-circuit. It sits at `:203`, before
`shouldHideForWidth` (`:212`) and the `runjobs` Job setup (`:227-241`). That bypass exists
today; changing it would change rendered output, and this phase's entire purpose is to
establish a baseline before output changes. File the width-hiding gap separately.

### A3. Warn and derive for unmarked files

A file without `version` is hand-written. Keep it working:

- Warn once per run, naming the file, saying it is neither hermetic nor deterministic, and
  giving the recorder command.
- For segments present in it, compute derived state so they stop silently vanishing.
- For segments absent from it, fall back to the live environment — the documented contract at
  `data.mdx:54-55`.

**[R] Where the derive happens matters.** Do **not** short-circuit at `:203` for this path.
Let `Execute` run normally so `Enabled()` fires at `:243` and then overlay the pinned data on
top. Short-circuiting at `:203` would skip `shouldHideForWidth` (`:212`), the `runjobs` Job
creation and its `defer` (`:227-241`) — so a pinned segment with a `timeout` would spawn live
child processes with no Job object, and `KillGoroutineChildren` could not terminate them on
Windows — and `segment.evaluated = true` at `:244`, leaving `renderFallback` (`:297`) dead.

Order is `Enabled()` then overlay, never the reverse. `json.Unmarshal` into the existing writer
preserves fields absent from the JSON, so pinned values win and derived values fill the gaps.

Add `--data-derive` to force this path for a recorded file too, for local debugging.

**[R] Note and document:** `restoreData` sets `Enabled = true` unconditionally, so a pinned
segment renders even where its live check would suppress it — `battery` on a machine without
one. That is today's behaviour and stays; say so in the docs rather than leaving it implicit.

### A4. Docs

Update `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx`: the recorder is the recommended path and the only
hermetic one; hand-written partial files still work and now derive correctly; the `version`
marker; the `alias` workaround for duplicate segment types.

**Verification:** `agnosterplus` with `{"time":{"CurrentDate":"2026-01-01T09:41:00Z"}}` renders
the time segment (it does not today). `chips` replayed from a re-recorded fixture makes **zero**
network calls and drops from 1.22s to the ~0.08s the other themes take. That timing is the
hermeticity proof — assert it, because the SSRF argument for any future render endpoint rests
on it.

---

## Task B — sanitized fixtures and the golden harness

**Owns:** the sanitizer, the harness test, the committed fixtures, and the `newEngine`
extraction below. Depends on Task A.

### B1. Sanitize structurally, not by string replace

**[R] A naive replace both corrupts and misses.** Case-insensitively replacing the username
rewrites `https://github.com/JanDeDobbeleer/oh-my-posh` in recorded git data into
`aliceDobbeleer`; case-sensitively, it misses `C:\Users\Jande` and `%USERNAME%` in caps.

And the identity is not confined to the `env` block. Recorded fixtures carry:

- `Segment.Text` — the fully rendered string, e.g. `" jande@surface-pro "`
- `git.User.Name` / `git.User.Email` — the real git author identity
- `aws.AccessKeyID`; `az` `TenantID`, `HomeTenantID`, subscription IDs, `User.Name` (an email)
- `path.Folders[].Path`, `git.Dir`, `env.AbsolutePWD` / `PSWD` / `Folder` — absolute paths in
  both `C:\Users\x` and `/c/Users/x` forms, and `~/…` after tilde replacement
- `sysinfo` real memory and load; `battery` real charge state
- the hostname, which is often a device model

So: a `--sanitize` flag on the recorder that (a) overwrites the `env` identity keys with
`alice` / `contoso-devbox` / `~/dev/oh-my-posh`, matching `website/segment_data.json` so the
fixtures and the website tell the same story; (b) clears every `Segment.Text`, which is
recomputed on render anyway; (c) applies a per-field scrub list covering the above; (d)
normalises `sysinfo` and `battery` to fixed values.

Keep a backstop test asserting no fixture contains the current user, host or home path, and a
denylist test for `AccessKeyID`, `User.Email` and `TenantID`. The backstop is not the mechanism
— it is what catches the next person regenerating on their own machine, before it reaches a
public repo.

### B2. The harness

**[R] `TestMain` must neutralise three ambient inputs, or this fails on CI immediately.**
`code.yml` runs `go test ./...` on ubuntu, macos and windows.

1. `time.Local = time.UTC`. 65 themes render a `time` segment through
   `dateInZone(fmt, date, "Local")` (`src/template/date.go:44`). Runners are UTC; a European
   contributor regenerating goldens shifts 65 files by an hour. Setting `TZ` is not reliable —
   verified no effect on Windows.
2. Unset `TERM_PROGRAM` and `WT_SESSION`, or set `terminal.Program` / `color.TrueColor`
   explicitly, before `terminal.Init`. Otherwise macOS Terminal.app emits 256-colour and every
   golden fails.
3. Point `cache.Path()` at a temp dir, and do not call `cache.Close()`. `segment.isToggled()`
   (`:424-437`) reads `TOGGLECACHE` from the session cache and returns *before* `restoreData`,
   so anyone who has ever run `oh-my-posh toggle` gets different goldens.

**[R] Do not call `prompt.New`.** It calls `config.Get`, which returns the session-cached config
and ignores the path entirely (`src/config/gob.go:44-49`) — inside any real omp shell, that is
the developer's own config. But hand-rolling the Engine the way `config_export_data.go:78-81`
does skips everything `New` performs after `config.Get`: `terminal.Plain`, `forceRender`,
`prompt.Grow(512)`, `flags.HasExtra`, and `rectifyTerminalWidth` for xonsh/elvish/pwsh
(`engine.go:836-860`) — so those branches would have no coverage.

Extract the post-`config.Get` half of `New` into `newEngine(cfg *config.Config, env
runtime.Environment) *Engine`, call it from both `New` and the harness, and have the harness use
`config.Load(path)` directly.

Then, for each of the **124** themes — enumerate by the same extension set
`export_themes.mjs:18` uses, `.omp.json`, `.omp.toml` and `.omp.yaml`; the two YAML themes go
through a different unmarshal path (`Segment.UnmarshalYAML`, `segment.go:133-155`) that would
otherwise have zero coverage — render and compare byte-for-byte against a committed golden.

- Failure output: first differing byte offset plus a decoded escape context window. A raw diff
  of two ANSI blobs is unreadable, and this harness exists to be read during a refactor.
- Regeneration is one documented command, named in the failure message.
- Goldens capture current output. This phase changes rendering only for the derive path, so
  expect `time`-pinned cases to change and nothing else. **[R]** Generate goldens once, then
  re-run — a second-run diff means non-determinism survived and is a stop-and-report.

**[R] Cost to state up front:** `themes/**` is not in any `paths-ignore`, so every theme-touching
PR now regenerates goldens. Recent gradient work would have. That is the price of the net.

---

## Task C — the website pipeline

**Owns:** `website/export_themes.mjs`.

**[R] Do not try to record `website/segment_data.json`.** It is circular: reproducing it needs a
machine with AWS, Azure, GCP, kubectl, Terraform, Cloud Foundry, Firebase, Strava, Spotify and
YouTube Music all simultaneously live and authenticated. That is why it is hand-written, and its
synthetic values are the point.

Under A3 it keeps working and warns. Pass `--data-derive` explicitly from `buildPoshCommand`
(`export_themes.mjs:179-193`) to state the intent and silence the warning. One line.

**[R] Separately:** `exportTheme` (`:236-241`) treats any stderr as "skip this theme", returns
`null`, and `main` still exits 0 — so a broken data file yields a silently empty themes page
rather than a red build. And `.github/workflows/docs.yml:3-9` only runs on push to `main`, while
`code.yml` and `build_code.yml` carry `paths-ignore: ['website/**']`, so nothing validates this
at PR time. Make a non-zero exit a hard failure.

---

## Task D — reset `isHyperlink`

**Owns:** `src/terminal/writer.go` and its tests. Independent; any order.

`isHyperlink` (`writer.go:78`) is set at `:460`, `:503`, `:562` and cleared only by encountering
`<TEXT>` (`:508`, `:567`). It is absent from both reset points — `Write`'s prologue
(`:385-392`) and `String()`'s deferred cleanup (`:605-619`). An unbalanced `<LINK>` therefore
leaves it `true` for the process lifetime, and every later `Write` takes the branch at
`:700-703`: runes go straight to the builder with no length counting and no shell escaping. The
`serve` daemon makes "process lifetime" a real exposure.

Reset it with the other per-render flags. Add a unit test writing an unbalanced `<LINK>` and
asserting the next `Write` counts length correctly.

**[R]** The first draft claimed the golden harness proves this inert. It does not — no bundled
theme uses `<LINK>`. The unit test is the whole proof, and D has no ordering dependency on B.

---

## Landing order

`A` → `B` → `C`. B's fixtures need A's format; C needs A3 in place. `D` is independent.

## Verification (coordinator, not delegated)

1. `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` clean from `src/`, on more than this machine's default env.
2. **Hermeticity:** `chips` replayed from a re-recorded fixture drops from 1.22s to ~0.08s and
   makes zero network calls. This is the load-bearing claim.
3. All 124 goldens pass, including both YAML themes. Corrupt one fixture and confirm the failure
   names the theme and shows a readable escape window.
4. Run the harness with `TZ` set to something other than UTC and with `TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal`
   — both must still pass, proving `TestMain` neutralises them.
5. Run with `POSH_SESSION_ID` set to a live session, proving the harness ignores the session cache.
6. `agnosterplus` with only `CurrentDate` pinned renders the time segment; an unmarked file warns.
7. Grep every committed fixture for the current user, host, home path, `AccessKeyID`,
   `User.Email`, `TenantID` — zero hits.
8. Benchmarks against the baseline: allocs/op and B/op unchanged. Ignore ns/op.
9. `npm run themes` still produces images for a sample of themes, and now fails loudly when a
   theme errors.

name: omp-data-replay-not-hermetic
description: "--data replay is not hermetic: the recorder skips disabled segments, so unrecorded ones still probe live"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Discovered 2026-07-26 while building a golden-file harness for the renderer work.

`oh-my-posh config export data` skips segments that were not enabled on the recording
machine (`src/cli/config_export_data.go:129-131`, `if !segment.Enabled { continue }`).
A fixture therefore covers only what happened to be live at record time; everything else
falls through `restoreData` (`src/config/segment.go:488-491` returns false) into the live
`writer.Enabled()` at `:243`. Measured: `themes/chips.omp.json` records 5 of 15 segments and
"replays" in **1.22s** because `wakatime` makes a real HTTP call, versus ~0.08s for themes
whose segments were all captured.

Two consequences that cost a full replan:

1. **Any "golden files over the bundled themes" measurement is suspect.** An early sweep
   showed 122/122 deterministic; that was an artifact — the fixture's pinned `PWD` does not
   exist, so every filesystem probe failed identically on both runs.
2. **The SSRF argument for a server-side render endpoint does not hold on replay alone.**
   `http`, `owm`, `nba`, `ipify`, `todoist` and `wakatime` all take a URL or key from config.
   Until the recorder captures every segment *and* `restoreData` suppresses recorded-but-
   disabled ones without probing, a data file is not a safety boundary.

Related: `restoreData` returns before `Enabled()`, and 53 of 102 segments assign
template-visible state inside `Enabled()` (≥24 of those do I/O). So a hand-written partial
file silently renders those segments empty — pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` drops
the whole rprompt block, because `Time.Format` is computed in `Enabled()`
(`src/segments/time.go:27-28`).

**Why:** three separate plans were built on "replay is hermetic" before it was measured.

**How to apply:** never treat a `--data` file as a hermetic or security boundary without
first checking the recorder covers every configured segment. Verify hermeticity by *timing*
a replay, not by diffing two runs — identical output can mean uniformly failing probes.
See [[omp-golden-harness-ambient-inputs]] for what else makes theme renders non-reproducible.

Found 2026-07-26 while scoping a golden-file harness over the bundled themes. Any test that
renders themes and compares bytes must neutralise all of these, or it fails on CI (which runs
ubuntu, macos and windows) while passing locally.

- **Local timezone.** `date` renders through `dateInZone(fmt, date, "Local")`
  (`src/template/date.go:44`), so a pinned absolute `CurrentDate` still prints in the
  renderer's zone — pinning `09:41:00Z` rendered `10:41:00` here. **65 of 124 themes** carry a
  `time` segment. Set `time.Local = time.UTC` in `TestMain`; setting `TZ` does not work on
  Windows.
- **`TERM_PROGRAM` / `WT_SESSION`.** `color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`
  (`src/terminal/writer.go:192`) gates truecolor versus 256-colour emission
  (`src/color/colors.go:312`). Same theme and fixture produce different bytes under
  macOS Terminal.app. Unset both, or set `terminal.Program` explicitly, before `terminal.Init`.
- **The session cache.** `segment.isToggled()` (`src/config/segment.go:424-437`) reads
  `TOGGLECACHE` and returns *before* `restoreData`, so anyone who has run `oh-my-posh toggle`

Good catch on the restoreCache ordering — you were right to flag it rather than silently fix or ignore it. I verified it, and it's a real regression that needs fixing before this lands. Please do so now.

The problem, confirmed: `restoreCache` at `src/config/segment.go:206-209` returns early on a cache hit (when not streaming), which skips your `overlayData()` at `:245`. Before your change, a hand-written entry short-circuited at `:202` and its pinned data always won. Now a live cache hit beats the pinned data.

It's reachable, and awkwardly so — I checked every bundled theme for a segment that is both pinned in `website/segment_data.json` and carries a `cache` block. Exactly one hit: `themes/chips.omp.json` -> `wakatime`. That is the same theme we use as the hermeticity proof. So the website's chips image could render a cached live WakaTime value instead of the pinned one, non-deterministically.

This breaks the explicit constraint on this task: hand-written files must keep working exactly as documented. So it has to be fixed, not just noted.

Suggested shape, but use your judgement since you have the full context:

    cacheRestored := segment.restoreCache()
    if cacheRestored && !env.Flags().Streaming {
        segment.overlayData()
        return
    }

That keeps "pinned data wins" without falling through to a live probe, so it stays hermetic and matches the pre-change behaviour. Check whether `overlayData` is safe to call on a cache-restored writer — if the restored state and the pinned overlay interact badly, say so and propose something else rather than forcing this shape.

Please add a regression test that covers it directly: a segment with a `cache` block, a warm cache, and a hand-written data file pinning a different value — assert the pinned value wins. Without that test this will regress again the next time someone reorders Execute.

Then re-run what you ran before: `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, golangci-lint, and the chips timing check (it must stay at roughly 0.08s, not climb back toward 1.2s). Report the diff, the test, and the timing.

`overlayData()` is safe to call here: `json.Unmarshal(segment.pendingData, &segment.writer)` only touches fields present in the pinned JSON, leaving the cache-restored writer's other fields untouched (same in-place-interface-unmarshal mechanism already used elsewhere in this file), and it's a no-op when `pendingData` is empty — the common case, no hand-written override for that segment. `restoreCache()` already called `template.Cache.AddSegmentData` with the same writer pointer, so the in-place mutation is visible through that cache reference without a second `AddSegmentData` call.

git add -A src/cli src/config website/docs/configuration/data.mdx && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(config): make recorded data replay hermetic

The data recorder skipped segments that were not enabled on the recording
machine, so a recorded file only covered whatever happened to be live at the
time. Everything else fell through to a live probe on replay. Recording
themes/chips.omp.json captured 5 of its 15 segments, and replaying it took
1.2 seconds because the unrecorded wakatime segment still made an HTTP
request. Replay was neither fast nor reproducible, and could not be used as a
boundary against segments that take a URL from config.

Record every configured segment along with whether it was enabled, and skip
the probe entirely for one recorded as disabled. The same theme now records
14 of 15 and replays in under 0.1s. The remaining gap is two text segments
sharing a data key, which the recorder already warns about.

Replaying a hand-written file was also dropping any state a segment computes
in Enabled(). Pinning the time segment's CurrentDate rendered nothing at all,
because Format is derived there, and losing the only segment in a block took
the block with it. Hand-written files are documented and stay supported, so
they now run the segment first and apply the pinned values over the result,
which also keeps width hiding and the job setup for segments with a timeout.
A file with no recorder marker says so once, and points at the command that
produces one.

Pinned values also have to survive a warm cache, which returns before the
overlay would otherwise run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
